sections.h2: What are my options to sell a house fast in Georgetown, TX?
sections.html:
A Georgetown owner can take a cash offer, list with an agent, or sell directly, and the choice depends on how much time, repair work and showing traffic you want to take on.

Georgetown is the county seat of Williamson County and one of the fastest-growing cities in the country by the Census Bureau's count. That growth brings steady buyer interest, but also many newly built homes competing with a resale. A cash buyer gives you a date and a price without showings, and a listing can reach buyers who want the house to be finished and staged.

  • Cash offer: as-is, flexible closing, minimal prep.
  • Listing: more exposure, more work, repair requests after inspection.
  • Direct sale: lower cost, but you manage paperwork and buyer screening.

sections.h2: How fast has Georgetown grown, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Very fast. The Census Bureau counted 47,400 people in 2010 and 67,176 in 2020, and estimates 106,907 for July 1, 2025, a 58.5 percent rise from the 2020 estimates base.

The same page shows 26.2 percent of residents aged 65 or older, 19.8 percent under 18 and 7,191 veterans for 2020 to 2024. A large older population means many owners are weighing downsizing, a move to be near family, or settling an estate. Those situations often favor a quick, low-effort sale, and they bring state tax rules for seniors and veterans into play, covered below.

The land area is 57.33 square miles at 1,171.7 people per square mile in 2020, so the city is spread out and commute times matter: the mean is 28.2 minutes.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Georgetown housing?
sections.html:
Georgetown is mostly owner-occupied with values near $429,100. The Census Bureau prints a 69.5 percent owner-occupied rate and a median gross rent of $1,795 for 2020 to 2024.

Owners with a mortgage have a median monthly cost of $2,328, and owners without a mortgage $895. If you carry a loan, a quick payoff estimate from your servicer is the first number to get, since it sets the floor for any offer.

sections.h2: Does Georgetown's historic downtown affect selling a house?
sections.html:
It can, if your house sits in or near the older neighborhoods around the Square. The city's visitor page says Georgetown has four National Register historic districts and 52 individually listed properties.

The city was founded in 1848, and its Public Square area is lined with Victorian and pre-World War I buildings, with the Williamson County Courthouse from 1911 at the center. Southwestern University, established in 1840, is also in town, and Lake Georgetown and the San Gabriel River trails are close by. Those features attract buyers who value older character homes and walkable streets.

  • Ask the city planning office whether your address is in a historic district or has design standards.
  • Tell buyers early about any exterior work you have done, with permits.
  • A cash buyer can purchase an older home as-is without the repair list a retail buyer might request.

sections.h2: How do homestead exemptions and the senior tax ceiling affect a Georgetown sale?
sections.html:
They matter because roughly a quarter of residents are 65 or older. School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and an additional $60,000 applies to owners aged 65 or older or disabled.

The school tax on a homestead of an owner who is 65 or older or disabled is generally frozen at the amount imposed in the year the owner first qualified. That ceiling can transfer proportionately to a new Texas homestead, though new improvements beyond repairs can raise it. A surviving spouse aged 55 or older may keep the benefit in certain cases. Cities, counties and junior college districts may adopt a similar limit.

Disabled veterans have separate exemptions, from up to $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating up to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent, and a total exemption on the homestead for 100 percent disabled veterans. Ask the Williamson Central Appraisal District which of these apply, and what a move would do to your ceiling.

sections.h2: What are the Georgetown property tax dates?
sections.html:
Taxes follow the statewide calendar. The appraisal district values every parcel as of January 1, and bills arrive around October 1.

  • Homestead appraisal notices go out around April 1.
  • Most protests are due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later.
  • The first half of a split payment is due November 30, and the second half June 30 of the following year.
  • Unpaid taxes are delinquent after January 31.

Appeals after the review board can go to district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the review board value is over $1,000,000. The Comptroller's pay page also notes that owners who appeal must generally pay the undisputed amount before the delinquency date.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Georgetown house, or title is unclear?
sections.html:
You can still sell, once title is documented. Heirs claiming a homestead exemption without a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

A transfer on death deed lets real property pass without probate, if it was recorded in the county before the owner died. The county clerk handles probate filings, small estate affidavits and deed recording. The Texas Courts clerk manual lists the recording fee as $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with extra clerk fees on top.

Gather the death certificate, the will if any, and any lender payoff statements before you speak to buyers.

faqs.q: Is Georgetown a good market for a quick house sale?
faqs.a: Demand is supported by rapid growth: the Census Bureau estimates 106,907 residents for 2025. Your own house, price and condition decide how fast it sells, so compare offers on net proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Georgetown?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $429,100 for owner-occupied units for 2020 to 2024. Use it only as a backdrop for your own offer or listing estimate.

faqs.q: Do seniors keep their school tax ceiling if they sell?
faqs.a: The ceiling can transfer proportionately to a new Texas homestead. Ask the appraisal district before you sign a contract.

faqs.q: Which county records my Georgetown deed?
faqs.a: Williamson County, since Georgetown is the county seat and the deed is recorded where the property sits.

faqs.q: Does the historic district matter if my house is newer?
faqs.a: Only if your address falls inside one. Ask the city planning office, and keep permit records for any exterior work.
